subject: MSA / Order Form: aligning governing law and narrow injunctive-relief carve
messages:

To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Price <michael.price@greenwave.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Draft redlines — governing law / injunctive relief (MSA)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Attached are our legal team's redlines to the MSA and order form. Two items they flagged as high priority before procurement can proceed:

1) Governing law / forum: they are pushing for California law (we are headquartered in SF) and the ability to seek injunctive relief locally.
2) Emergency relief carve: they want explicit language that allows them to get temporary injunctive or preservation relief in California courts while any monetary claims go to arbitration.

We understand many vendors prefer a single governing law and arbitration for disputes — happy to find middle ground. For timeline, procurement is hoping for a path to sign by the end of next week if we can land language that preserves their ability to get emergency relief locally.

I've attached the redline PDF (Greenwave_MSA_redlines_20260321.pdf) and a short note from counsel. Can you confirm Redwood's position and proposed compromise language?

Thanks,
Anita Desai
Head of Legal Operations
Greenwave Systems

Subject: Re: Draft redlines — governing law / injunctive relief (MSA)

Anita —

Appreciate the clear callouts and the quick turnaround. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (account lead) to work through concrete language.

High‑level from us: Redwood prefers a single governing law and a streamlined dispute-resolution path (arbitration) for monetary claims. That said, we are open to a narrow, temporary-relief carve that allows a customer to seek provisional injunctive measures in a local court to preserve the status quo (e.g., stop a deletion or protect confidential data) while the rest of the dispute proceeds to arbitration.

Before we draft, two clarifying questions:
- Is Greenwave asking for an exclusive right to sue in California for emergency relief (i.e., permanently conferring venue for all injunctive matters), or a limited preservation-only route?
- Is there any regulatory/regulatory enforcement concern that would require a specific law seat beyond commercial preference?

Kimberly — can you draft two short alternatives: (A) governing law = New York; arbitration for monetary claims; limited preservation injunctive-relief carve for local courts (expressly temporary and non-waiving); (B) governing law = California but with an expedited arbitration carve for monetary relief and a mutual injunctive-relief reservation. We'll present both to Greenwave.

Marissa — heads up the timeline: procurement wants to move quickly if we can land language.

Rishi
Head of Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Draft redlines — governing law / injunctive relief (MSA)

Rishi/Anita —

Thanks for the overview. Attached is a short proposed compromise (RW-proposed-injunction-clause.docx) and the text pasted below so it's easier to review in-thread. We kept the drafting targeted to preserve Greenwave's ability to obtain temporary injunctive relief while protecting Redwood's operational and arbitration expectations. Two alternatives are shown; my recommendation is Alternative A as it is narrower and harder to litigate around.

--- Proposed language (summary) ---
Alternative A (recommended):
1) Governing law: The Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict of law principles.
2) Dispute resolution: Except for the narrow preservation relief described below, all disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the rules mutually agreed upon.
3) Preservation relief carve: Either party may seek temporary injunctive or other provisional relief in a court of competent jurisdiction solely for the purpose of preserving the status quo or preventing imminent, irreparable harm (e.g., to protect confidential data, stop deletion of data, or prevent unauthorized access). Such relief is temporary in nature, does not determine substantive rights, and pursuing such relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the arbitration agreement for monetary claims. Venue for preservation relief may be a court where the party seeking relief has its principal place of business.

Alternative B (if customer insists on law seat parity):
1) Governing law: The Agreement will be governed by the laws of the State of California.
2) Dispute resolution: All monetary disputes shall be resolved by binding arbitration. Either party may seek provisional injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction.

Practical notes:
- Keep preservation language narrowly tailored (time-limited; limited remedies) to avoid forum-shopping.
- Add a short mutual acknowledgement that courts’ provisional remedies are not inconsistent with the arbitration clause.
- We can also add a short escalation step (30-day negotiation/managed-dispute pathway) for enterprise customers prior to filing where appropriate.

If Greenwave prefers Alternative B, we should also define an expedited arbitration timeline (e.g., emergency arbitrator + 90-day panel decision) to reduce customer concern about delay on monetary relief.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Kimberly/Rishi —

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of practical compromise we were hoping for. Greenwave prefers Alternative A (New York law + narrow preservation carve) so long as the preservation carve clearly permits temporary relief in California courts when necessary and confirms that it is strictly limited to provisional measures. That solves the procurement team's primary concern.

Next steps for us: I'll run the proposed clause by our GC this morning and get back with any final tweaks. If the language is acceptable we can aim to exchange final markups and get an approved order form signed by Friday.

Can you drop the agreed text into the shared Drive doc and send a DocuSign link once both sides confirm? HubSpot ticket HS-0042217 will be updated with the final draft.

Appreciate the quick collaboration — happy to close this this week.
